It wires a NetworkPolicy informer into the operator lifecycle, implements sync logic to apply four static NetworkPolicies to the MCO namespace, adds a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy preventing deletion of managed policies, and includes comprehensive unit and e2e tests validating the behavior. ## Changes **NetworkPolicy Management for Machine Config Operator** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**NetworkPolicy Informer Integration**
`pkg/operator/operator.go`, `cmd/machine-config-operator/start.go`|Operator struct gains `networkPolicyInformerSynced` cache sync flag; `New` constructor accepts `NetworkPolicyInformer` parameter; informer registered with shared informers, cache sync tracked in `Run()`, and a "NetworkPolicies" sync step inserted into the reconciliation sequence; start command passes the namespaced informer from the factory.| |**NetworkPolicy Sync Implementation**
`pkg/operator/network_policy.go`|Implements `Operator.syncNetworkPolicies` method and builder helpers that construct server-side apply configurations for four static NetworkPolicies: default-deny (empty podSelector, no ingress/egress rules), allow-machine-config-operator, allow-machine-config-controller, and allow-machine-os-builder (each allowing TCP 9001 ingress and all egress); applies all four unconditionally to MCO namespace with server-side apply using fixed field manager and Force=true.| |**Deletion Guard Protection**
`manifests/machineconfigcontroller/networkpolicy-deletion-guard-validatingadmissionpolicy.yaml`, `manifests/machineconfigcontroller/networkpolicy-deletion-guard-validatingadmissionpolicybinding.yaml`, `pkg/operator/sync.go`|Adds ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that denies DELETE operations on namespaced NetworkPolicies in MCO namespace unless name is in allowlist (default-deny, allow-machine-config-operator, allow-machine-config-controller, allow-machine-os-builder); ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding sets Deny validation action; manifests registered in `syncMachineConfigController` baseline validating admission policies.| |**Unit Tests**
`pkg/operator/network_policy_test.go`|Tests validate all four policies are created unconditionally; default-deny has empty podSelector and no ingress/egress rules; each allow policy has correct `k8s-app` label selector, exactly one ingress rule targeting TCP 9001 with no From restriction, and one egress rule allowing all; machine-os-builder always created regardless of pool state; syncNetworkPolicies is idempotent.| |**End-to-End Tests**
`test/e2e-2of2/network_policy_test.go`|Validates all four managed policies exist with correct selectors and rules; tests operator reconciliation by modifying and verifying restoration of ingress rules; validates deletion protection via admission policy denial; confirms machine-config ClusterOperator health and MCO pods remain Running; tests that manual modifications to default-deny are reverted; validates user-created policies coexist with managed policies while retaining their configuration.| ## Sequence Diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Operator participant NetworkPolicyInformer as NetworkPolicy Informer participant SyncCycle as Sync Cycle participant ServerSideApply as Server-Side Apply participant KubeAPI as Kubernetes API participant AdmissionPolicy as Validating Admission Policy Operator->>NetworkPolicyInformer: Register watch NetworkPolicyInformer->>NetworkPolicyInformer: Cache sync SyncCycle->>SyncCycle: Wait for cache ready SyncCycle->>SyncCycle: Call syncNetworkPolicies SyncCycle->>ServerSideApply: Apply 4 policies (default-deny, allow-mco, allow-mcc, allow-mob) ServerSideApply->>KubeAPI: Server-side apply Force=true KubeAPI->>KubeAPI: Update NetworkPolicies Note over KubeAPI,AdmissionPolicy: DELETE attempt on managed policy KubeAPI->>AdmissionPolicy: Validate DELETE AdmissionPolicy-->>KubeAPI: Deny (not allowlisted) ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~30 minutes

Hello, I'm experimenting with an agent I've created to do adversarial testing

This is the analysis


```
  Critical Bugs                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  1. VAP blocks operator's own MOB policy deletion (Critical)
  - pkg/operator/network_policy.go:92 calls Delete("allow-machine-os-builder") when no layered pools exist                               
  - networkpolicy-deletion-guard-validatingadmissionpolicy.yaml:20 explicitly blocks deletion of allow-machine-os-builder                      
  - The VAP binding has no exemption for the MCO service account             
  - Impact: If a cluster removes all layered pools, the operator enters a permanent Degraded state. Verified on live cluster.
  - Fix: Exclude allow-machine-os-builder from the VAP, or add a CEL exemption for the MCO service account                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  2. SSA doesn't revert modifications to default-deny (High)                                                                              
  - pkg/operator/network_policy.go:19-24 — defaultDenyNetworkPolicy only declares PodSelector and PolicyTypes, but not Ingress/Egress                                                                              
  - SSA only manages fields it declares. An attacker can add ingress rules to default-deny and the operator never reverts them                                                                                    
  - Since default-deny uses an empty podSelector, added ingress rules open traffic to all pods                                                                                                                     
  - Fix: Add explicit empty WithIngress() and WithEgress() to the apply configuration                                
                                                                                                                              
  3. NetworkPolicy sync failure blocks entire operator sync chain (High)
  - pkg/operator/sync.go:204-216 — syncAll breaks on first error
  - If syncNetworkPolicies fails (e.g., from Issue 1), syncMachineConfigController, syncMachineConfigServer, syncMachineOSBuilder, and syncRequiredMachineConfigPools never run                                    
  - Impact: A narrow network policy failure causes total operator failure                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                         
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Design Gaps                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  4. Rogue policies not cleaned up (Medium)                                                            
  - syncNetworkPolicies only applies its known policies — it never lists existing ones to remove unknown policies
  - Any user with NetworkPolicy write access can create an allow-all policy that permanently bypasses default-deny
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  5. Sync order: policies created before VAP exists (Low)                                                                                                                                                          
  - On first sync cycle, network policies are at position 6, VAP deploys at position 8                                                                                                                             
  - Brief window where policies are unprotected on fresh installs                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  Test Gaps                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                         
  6. No test covers MOB cleanup with VAP active (Medium)
  - Unit test TestSyncNetworkPolicies_MOBPolicyDeletedWithoutLayeredPools uses fake.NewClientset() (no VAP admission)
  - No e2e test covers the transition from layered→non-layered pools     
  - This is exactly how Issue 1 went undetected                 
```
